questions.question: From what age are you allowed to start learning to drive in Iceland?
questions.explanation: Learning may begin at 16, which is two years before the age at which the full category B entitlement is normally used independently.

questions.question: What must a learner obtain before the driving course can begin?
options: A medical certificate issued by a doctor
A temporary licence issued by the police
An insurance policy in the learner's name
A permit issued by a District Commissioner
questions.explanation: The learner's permit comes from the District Commissioner; only after that does instruction with a driving instructor start.

questions.question: During a driving lesson, who is legally considered the operator of the car?
options: The learner, because the learner steers
The registered owner of the vehicle
The owner of the driving school
questions.explanation: Legal responsibility for the vehicle rests with the instructor during a lesson, even though the learner is doing the actual driving.

questions.question: How many driving lessons is a learner generally assumed to take before starting accompanied practice driving?
questions.explanation: Ten lessons is the general assumption, but the instructor is the one who judges when the learner is actually ready.

questions.question: Why must a car used for accompanied practice driving carry the practice-driving label?
options: So the police can check the learner's permit
So the learner is exempt from some traffic rules
So the car is identified as a driving school car
So other drivers can give the learner room
questions.explanation: The label is a warning to surrounding traffic, not a permit or an exemption; other drivers use it to leave safe space for the learner.

questions.question: What is the minimum age of the person who supervises accompanied practice driving?
questions.explanation: The supervising practice-driving instructor must be at least 24 and also hold several years of driving experience.

questions.question: What does research say about using a hands-free phone while driving?
options: It removes the risk of an accident
It still raises the risk of an accident
It is as safe as talking to a passenger
It only distracts drivers in heavy traffic
questions.explanation: The distraction is mental rather than manual, so the accident risk stays elevated even when both hands remain on the wheel.

questions.question: Learning to drive covers three main areas: knowledge, skill and what else?
questions.explanation: Attitude covers how the driver behaves towards others; courtesy and understanding are treated as learnable parts of the course.

questions.question: What is the maximum authorised mass of a car that may be driven on a category B licence?
questions.explanation: Category B is limited to 3,500 kg; anything heavier requires a licence of a higher category such as C1 or C.

questions.question: How should a driver understand the right of way in traffic?
options: As an absolute right others must respect
As a priority, never as an absolute right
As a rule that applies only at signed junctions
As belonging to whoever reaches the spot first
questions.explanation: Priority never entitles a driver to press on regardless; assuming what another road user will do is how collisions happen.

questions.question: On a category B licence, when may you tow a trailer heavier than 750 kg?
options: When the trailer carries no passengers at all
When the trailer has its own braking system
When car and trailer together stay within 3,500 kg
When you have held the licence for two years
questions.explanation: The 750 kg trailer limit can be exceeded only while the combined authorised mass of car and trailer remains within 3,500 kg.

questions.question: What is the highest design speed of a moped that may be ridden on a category B licence?
questions.explanation: A light motorcycle covered by category B is limited to 45 km/h design speed and 50 cubic centimetres of cylinder capacity.

questions.question: Which body runs the theoretical and practical driving tests in Iceland?
questions.explanation: Testing is handled by one of the vehicle inspection companies, Frumherji, for every licence category.

questions.question: How long is the provisional licence valid after you pass the driving test?
questions.explanation: The first licence is provisional for three years, after which it is replaced by the permanent licence.

questions.question: Once you hold a permanent driving licence, how often must it be renewed?
questions.explanation: The right to drive itself is unlimited in time, but the licence document has to be renewed at 15-year intervals.

questions.question: What happens if a driving licence stays unrenewed for more than two years after it expires?
options: The licence is renewed against a higher fee
A medical examination replaces the renewal
The driving test must be taken again
The holder reverts to a provisional licence
questions.explanation: After more than two years of lapse the entitlement is no longer simply renewable and the test has to be passed again.

questions.question: A provisional driver who is penalised for a traffic offence may apply for the permanent licence only after what?
options: Paying the fine and a renewal fee
Taking additional lessons with an instructor
questions.explanation: The clock restarts: a full penalty-free year is required, and failing to achieve it within two years means retaking the driving test.

questions.question: Which item is a driver required to carry in the car when driving in France?
questions.explanation: Rules differ from country to country, and France is the example given of a state requiring a breath alcohol tester on board.

questions.question: Roughly what share of the information a driver uses is taken in through the eyes?
questions.explanation: Because sight supplies about nine tenths of the information, anything that degrades vision has a large effect on driving.

questions.question: How are medicines that may impair driving marked in Iceland?
options: A red triangle on a white background
A red circle on a yellow background
A black cross on a white background
A blue square on a white background
questions.explanation: The red warning triangle flags drugs that can cause drowsiness; when unsure, ask a doctor or pharmacist before driving.
